resources.string: "Average smoothing algorithm, newest value is not affected"
"No smoothing performed on input glucose data. Use this when you already have filtered data e.g. from BYODA G6."

Fractional weight of the first-order value (faster, less smooth) to use in the smoothed result value. The second-order contribution is one minus this fractional weight. A lower fractional weight here results in a more responsive but less smooth BGL curve, while a higher value will be smoother but less responsive (more delay). Default 0.4.

Parameter \'a\' in the first-order smoothing calculation. Determines the fraction of previous BG delta to be added to obtain the next BG value. Higher values are more responsive but less smooth. Default 0.5.

Parameter \'a\' in the second-order smoothing calculation. Determines the weighting of the direct glucose reading, versus (previous reading + delta). Higher values are more responsive, but less smooth. Default 0.4.

Parameter \'b\' in the second-order smoothing calculation. Determines the weighting of the current smoothed glucose difference in computing the BG delta, versus the previous BG delta. A value of 1.0 uses only the current smoothed glucose difference as the delta (most responsive). Lower values give more contribution from previous delta values. Default 1.0.

The filter\'s white noise suppression parameter. Higher values more closely match the original BGs; lower values provide more smoothing. Default 0.4. Recommended range 0.2 (very noisy data) to 0.6 (for very good BG data with very little noise).
Degree of the filter kernel. Should be 2, 4, 8 or 10; any values outside this will be rounded up to the nearest supported degree. Default 10. It is not recommended to change this.
